description_full: First Community Bankshares, Inc. operates as the financial holding company for First Community Bank that provides various banking products and services. It offers demand and savings deposits, money market accounts, certificates of deposit, and individual retirement accounts; commercial loans, such as loans to small and mid-size industrial, commercial, and service companies; and consumer real estate loans, including home equity loans, lines of credit, and financing residential properties. The company also provides consumer and other loans comprising automobile, credit cards, personal lines of credit, boats, mobile homes, and other consumer goods; and trust management, estate administration, and investment advisory services. It serves individual and commercial customers in the education, government, health services, retail trade, construction, manufacturing, tourism, coal mining and gas extraction, and transportation industries. The company operates through branches in Virginia, West Virginia, North Carolina, and Tennessee. First Community Bankshares, Inc. was founded in 1874 and is headquartered in Bluefield, Virginia.

financial_summary: First Community Bankshares, Inc is a small-cap financial services business with a $861M market cap on $168M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +4% over the past three years and +4% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 10% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically.

The business throws off $60M in free cash flow — roughly 36 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.29× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.0× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 3.8×.

Management returns a meaningful 7.3% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 16% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
